newsitem.title: USA: Colgate shares up on dividend, stock split.
newsitem.headline: Colgate shares up on dividend, stock split.

text.p: Colgate-Palmolive Co shares rose more than two points Thursday as the company set a two-for-one stock split and boosted its quarterly dividend by 17 percent.
Colgate was trading around 108-3/4 late Thursday, up 2-1/8 on the day. Earlier in the afternoon the stock briefly edged past its 52-week high of 109-1/4 before falling back.
Increasing the dividend to $0.55 from $0.47 "illustrates the company's own conviction about its long-term growth," said Michael Grant, a J.P. Morgan analyst.
That is a conviction Grant himself shares: "Colgate has been my No. 1 pick for 1997. It's got great prospects for the year."
Constance Maneaty, a Bear Stearns analyst, said she regarded the action as routine, since healthy companies regularly raise their dividends and split their stock.
Colgate "is a good company," she said. "They're trying to get leaner. They're doing a good job at the moment."
Colgate said it generated cash at a record clip in 1996, and returned much of it to shareholders.

"With this latest increase, Colgate's dividend has grown at a compound rate of 16 percent over the past five years, supporting our firm commitment to increase shareholder value," said Reuben Mark, Colgate's chairman and chief executive, in the statement announcing the dividend increase and stock split.
Colgate said the price of its stock has appreciated 178 percent since its last two-for-one split in May 1991, compared to a 118 percent increase for the S&P 500 index over the same period.
The company also recommended for shareholder approval an increase in its common stock to one billion shares from 500 million.
Colgate's products include Colgate toothpaste, Palmolive soap, Ajax detergent and Speed Stick deodorant.
